ai.title: excludeToolFromMessageHistory flag gates tool result logging
ai.summary: Added `excludeToolFromMessageHistory` boolean to `ExecuteToolCallParams` and threaded through `runProgrammaticStep`. When `includeToolCall` is false, assistant tool call messages and subsequent tool result pushes to `state.messages` are skipped. Removes unused `agentType` param from `runProgrammaticStep` and `loopAgentSteps`. Covers backend `tools/tool-executor.ts`, `run-programmatic-step.ts`, `run-agent-step.ts`.

eli5.text: The tool you use now has a switch to decide whether its results get recorded in the conversation history. When that switch is set to 'no,' the system skips logging the tool's action and its outcome into the running transcript. This affects any workflow that toggles that switch off, so those tool activities simply won't appear in the stored conversation trail.

ai.title: Preserve spawned context during truncation
ai.summary: Added keepDuringTruncation flag to createConversationHistoryMessage in spawn-agent-utils.ts. Ensures spawned agent context survives conversation history trimming. Internal backend change.

eli5.text: When a conversation gets too long and the system has to trim older parts to stay within its memory limit, it now makes sure to keep the context that was set up when a helper agent was spawned. This affects the assistant's behavior behind the scenes: spawned agent context survives conversation history trimming. You wouldn't notice this directly, since it's internal housekeeping that prevents important background context from being lost during long conversations.

ai.title: Planner gains read-only-commander, editor model updated
ai.summary: Planner agent now includes `read-only-commander` subagent to find files via absolute paths and read 20+ files for better context. Editor agent model updated from `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. Instructions updated to prioritize user message over plan. Files: `.agents/base2/editor.ts`, `.agents/base2/planner-factory.ts`.

eli5.text: The planning assistant now brings in a helper that can open and read dozens of files at once to gather better background before writing up a plan, and the editing assistant switched to a newer version of its underlying model. If you watched a planning session, you'd notice the resulting plan reflects more of the codebase because the planner pulled in more file contents. The editor is now a bit more conversational, treating your original message as the most important reference instead of strictly following the plan. These changes are live today for anyone who uses these internal assistants.

ai.title: Fix prompt caching for Sonnet models
ai.summary: Added `shouldCacheModels` array in `common/src/old-constants.ts` to explicitly enable prompt caching for specific Anthropic models (Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4, etc.). Updated `getExplicitlyDefinedModels` in `common/src/util/model-utils.ts` to include these new entries in the allowed set. This ensures prompt caching works correctly for Sonnet models referenced by their short OpenRouter names.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant with a Sonnet model accessed through its short OpenRouter name, the assistant will now correctly remember and reuse your earlier conversation prompts instead of treating each message as brand-new. Without this fix, the model was being told not to cache prompts by default, which made responses slower and less consistent. The change adds the relevant model names to an explicit allowlist that turns prompt caching back on for them. This is live today for anyone using those specific Anthropic model references.

ai.title: Add 5% fudge factor to judge context limit
ai.summary: MAX_TOKENS in evals/git-evals/judge-git-eval.ts now applies a 0.95 multiplier to the 1 million token cap. This introduces a 5% margin to prevent judge context overflow during eval runs. Scope limited to git evals judge logic.

eli5.text: The automated judge that evaluates git-based coding tasks now leaves about 5% of its reasoning space unused. This reduces the chance that a complex analysis will run out of room mid-evaluation. You would only notice this through fewer overflow errors in the background scoring process; it does not change any visible interface or output format.

constants.name: MAX_TOKENS
constants.to: 1_000_000 * 0.95 // 1 million token limit, with 5% fudge factor

ai.summary: read-only-commander model switched to openai/gpt-5-chat. Planner pre-checks file existence via read_files before reading, filtering non-existent paths. Base2 prompts updated to emphasize upfront instruction density. Changes confined to .agents/base2 internal factories.

eli5.text: The internal helper that assists with code tasks now uses a newer AI model to review files, and it double-checks that files exist before trying to read them. The planner agent now filters out non-existent file paths before reading, avoiding errors. These changes are internal and affect how the assistant processes requests behind the scenes.

ai.title: README SDK section restructured with custom agent example
ai.summary: README.md SDK section retitled to 'Run agents in production' with numbered code comments and a custom AgentDefinition example. Adds `agentDefinitions` param usage with `id`, `displayName`, `model`, `instructionsPrompt` fields. Cosmetic formatting fixes (blank lines around code fences) in CLI install section.

eli5.text: The project's instruction manual for building AI tools was rewritten: the section about making AI agents work in real projects is now called 'Run agents in production,' and it shows step-by-step how to set one up, including an example of creating a custom AI assistant with a name, display label, model choice, and custom instructions. If you opened the manual, you'd see numbered comments guiding you through starting a simple coding task and then defining a personalized agent you can tweak. This change is live today and only affects anyone reading the manual.
